why: Copy a person reads that is still written in the code rather than in _locales. Every entry is debt with an owner: B-75 carries the translation work, and the shape it must take is named there — a core package returns facts, the surface words them, because core-* packages have no dependencies and adding @okolos/i18n to them would spend that property on a string table.
rule: Exact match. A file with more hits than its entry is a regression; a file with fewer means the debt was paid and the number here has to come down in the same change. Both are refusals, because a ceiling nobody lowers is a ceiling that rots upward.
paidSoFar: core-recovery closed 2026-08-20: 18 step sentences and 6 portable lines moved to _locales. The package keeps the id, the order and `elsewhere` — the facts it actually decides — and `packages/ui/src/recovery/recovery.ts` maps id to key through two `*_KEY` tables, which is the shape the locale gate reads: a computed key would make all eighteen messages look dead to it. The assertions about the words moved to the surface's test rather than being deleted with the words. core-download closed the same day: five headlines and five shape sentences became codes, and the codes now cross the `download/verdict` RPC — the background used to compose English and send it. `reasons` deliberately stayed words, because those come from the checks and whoever ran them had already resolved them through the catalogue. core-credential closed the same day: seven credential facts and five password explanations became codes, and one of them had been formatting a number with `toLocaleString('en')` — an English thousands separator chosen inside a package with no business knowing the reader's locale, and invisible to this sweep because it is not a quoted string. The count travels as a number now. core-gate and core-extensions closed 2026-08-20. The gate's `explain` was a finished sentence beside a `reason` that already said the same thing as a code, so the sentence is gone rather than moved: `describes` carries the action, `detail` the browser's own words about a surface that would not open, and `apps/extension/src/background/gate-words.ts` words the seven reasons. core-extensions gave up five change sentences, two analysis caveats and a hex density that arrived as English prose with the number already inside it — `InventoryChange` is a discriminated union now, so a `host-access-widened` without its hosts fails to compile instead of rendering a sentence with a hole in it, and the wording lives behind a second export path, `@okolos/ui/words`, because two surfaces need the same sentence and pulling the whole UI graph into the worker for a lookup table is not a trade worth making. Both write `explainKey` + `explainArgs` into the journal rather than a resolved sentence: `summarise` in the popup resolves at read time, so a reader who switches language sees their own words on old rows — and the extensions journal's dedup, which used to compare the sentence, compares those values, or a change of language alone would rewrite every unaccepted row and push `createdAt` to today. Two blind spots in the sweep were found by reading rather than by the tool, and both are recorded as B-76: a sentence whose first word ends in a colon (`'Blocked: this page…'`) breaks the three-word anchor, and a nested quote inside a template substitution (`` `${n} thing${n === 1 ? '' : 's'} worth a look.` ``) truncates the literal before the sentence starts. The second one was live in `packages/ui/src/extensions/extensions.ts` and is fixed here; the ceiling never counted either of them, which is the point of the row.
